answer: Identity must wander through a mirror before it earns a vote. A newcomer submits a signed traversal of an audit graph whose every hop is countersigned by a distinct established party, and the resulting traversal hash is published, so two aliases routed through the same parties collide on one mirror and collapse into a single identity. Each mirror inscription costs its index squared in escrow, so n heads need n distinct signers and roughly n cubed in bond. A comet beacon randomly replays one hop per epoch; failing the replay voids every identity sharing that mirror.
